newsitem.title: GERMANY: ProSieben promises generous dividends after float.
newsitem.headline: ProSieben promises generous dividends after float.

text.p: German television group ProSieben Media AG, which plans to float on the Frankfurt stock exchange in July, said on Thursday that sales and profits grew both in 1996 and in the first quarter of this year.

With just over a month before ProSieben's stock market debut -- the first by a German broadcaster -- growing profits enabled chief executive Georg Kofler to dangle the prospect of generous dividends to investors.
Management at the company was made up of people "with a certain tendency towards generosity to shareholders", Kofler told a news conference called to announce 1996 results.
ProSieben Media AG, which runs the ProSieben and Kabel 1 commercial television channels, posted group sales of 1.69 billion marks ($996.6 million) last year, up from 1.47 billion marks.
ProSieben ranks behind RTL and SAT1 as Germany's third largest commercial station, pulling in around one-tenth of the viewing public and a bigger share in advertising revenues.
Net profits jumped to 169 million marks from 96 million the year before, while group income from ordinary activities rose to 178 million marks from 111 million.
Another indicator of the group's improved profitability was a rise last year in its pre-tax return on sales to 10 percent from 7.6 percent.
Group sales were up 17.5 percent in the first quarter of this year to 479 million marks, while pre-tax profits rose to 84 million marks from 63 million a year earlier.
The company said it expected significant increases in both sales and pre-tax profits this year.
ProSieben Media AG is currently owned outright by Thomas Kirch, son of powerful Bavarian media magnate Leo Kirch -- a champion of digital pay television in Germany -- and the Rewe retail group.

Kofler said that a price range for the issue of 17.5 million preferred shares would be announced on June 23. The share offer would be open to investors from the next day, with subscriptions closing on July 3. The first listing on the Frankfurt stock exchange is planned for July 7.
Banks will also have a so-called "greenshoe option" to buy an additional 1.75 million shares if the issue is heavily subscribed.
Kofler said that the ProSieben dividend on preferred shares would be 0.15 marks above the payout for ordinary stock.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.695 German Marks)
